[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Arthur was born in 1809. He was the son of [[Glasgow-653|Joseph Glasgow]]. He passed away in 1852.
== Research Notes ==
=== Father identification ===

[[Glasgow-653|Joseph Glasgow]] is confidently inferred to be this person’s father, assessed 95%. Arthur is already explicitly assigned to Joseph in the compiled account with Faris p. 34. The memoir supplies an additional distinctive sibling role: the California forty-niner who drowned returning. The family group supports that identification. An Ohio probate estate does not by itself establish a contradictory physical place of death; the drowning and probate identity still merit checking. <ref name="Miami1919">John C. Hover et al., eds., ''Memoirs of the Miami Valley'' (Robert O. Law Company, 1919–1920), “S. S. Glasgow,” printed pp. 257–258; [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18001/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 257] and [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18002/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 258], Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library Digital Library; images inspected 22 October 2026. Published family biography, not a civil or parish register.</ref>

The memoir never names Joseph: its sibling group is linked to [[Glasgow-1625|Robert Anderson]], whose 1880 county biography names Joseph and Nancy. The memoir’s ancestral migration story is inconsistent with Joseph’s Virginia birth, and Eliza/Breckenridge appears to be a Campbell half-sister. These problems qualify the whole-pair inference; no mother or vital fact is changed. The 1880 statement is used from its published citation and held biographical account, not a newly inspected image.


=== Earlier father assessment, 22 October 2026 — superseded ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-653]] is assessed at 93% (proved). The held Arthur account explicitly names Joseph as father and cites Faris p34. Arthur’s 1809 Adams County birth follows Joseph’s 1780 generation within the same documented descendant family, providing a specific compiled household identification.

Compiled-family attribution93%; the original book evidence and probate relationship wording were not newly inspected.

Next useful test: Check Arthur’s probate and Faris’s source references.

Source basis already held: [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990); specific retained family statements and page citations identified in each reviewed pair]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
